source: CK-12 Chemistry Concepts Intermediate, Section 10.1, CC-BY-NC
notes: Class B document (13 units). Fourth chemistry document. Covers conservation of mass and the balancing procedure with a worked example. One ECU for the worked example.

units.label: Hook: unbalanced scale image (image)
units.content_summary: Photo of an unbalanced two-pan scale, one side heavier than the other. Caption: 'A chemical equation is like a scale — both sides must balance.'

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: state the law of conservation of mass; identify reactants and products in an equation; balance a simple chemical equation using coefficients.

units.label: Law of conservation of mass (text)
units.content_summary: Matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction — the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products. This means the number of atoms of each element must be the same on both sides of the equation.

units.label: Anatomy of an equation (text)
units.content_summary: Reactants (starting substances) on the left, products (resulting substances) on the right, separated by an arrow. Coefficients (numbers in front of formulas) show how many molecules of each substance react/form; subscripts show atoms within a molecule and cannot be changed.

units.label: Equation anatomy diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Labeled diagram of the equation 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, with arrows pointing out 'coefficient', 'reactants', 'products', and 'subscript' on the relevant parts.

units.label: Balancing procedure (text)
units.content_summary: Step-by-step procedure: (1) count atoms of each element on both sides; (2) add coefficients (never change subscripts) to make counts equal; (3) start with the most complex molecule; (4) recheck all elements after each change.

units.label: Worked example: methane combustion (text)
units.content_summary: Balance: CH4 + O2 → CO2 + H2O. Step-by-step: C balances (1=1); H needs 4 on right → 2H2O; O now needs 4 on left → 2O2. Final balanced equation: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Verified atom-by-atom.

units.label: Worked example atom-count table (image)
units.content_summary: Before/after table showing atom counts for C, H, O on each side of the methane combustion equation, confirming all counts match after balancing.

units.label: Video: balancing walkthrough (video)
units.content_summary: Video walking through balancing a second example (photosynthesis equation) step by step, showing coefficient adjustments and atom recounts in real time.

units.label: Common mistakes (text)
units.content_summary: Common errors: changing subscripts instead of adding coefficients (this changes the substance's identity, not just its quantity); forgetting to recheck all elements after each adjustment.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Four unbalanced equations to balance: H2 + O2 → H2O; Fe + O2 → Fe2O3; N2 + H2 → NH3; Na + Cl2 → NaCl.
